orientation.central_question: How do qualitative research methods help an IS manager investigate how and why organisational phenomena happen?
orientation.one_sentence_answer: Qualitative research studies meaning in natural settings through four overarching methods, three data collection techniques, and four explicit quality tests.
takeaways: A method is an overarching strategy; an interview is only a data collection technique.
The four methods differ in unit of analysis and engagement model.
Quality is argued through credibility, dependability, transferability, and confirmability.

concepts.title: Methodology as strategy
concepts.statement: A methodology is a strategy of inquiry chosen to answer a research question, and it can be qualitative, quantitative, or mixed.
details: The words versus numbers split is useful but narrow.
concepts.recall_cue: What does a method actually decide?
concepts.source_heading: 1. Research methodology and the qualitative distinction

concepts.title: Technique is not method
concepts.statement: An interview is a data collection technique and a questionnaire is part of a survey method, so neither is a method on its own.
details: Confusing the two collapses design into data collection.
concepts.source_heading: 1. Research methodology and the qualitative distinction

concepts.title: Grounded theory
concepts.statement: Grounded theory discovers theory from systematically obtained data, reversing the traditional order by collecting data before proposing a theory.
details: Choose it to explain a process or stay close to the data.

concepts.title: Three coding stages
concepts.statement: Open coding labels phenomena, axial coding interconnects the categories, and selective coding builds the connecting story into propositions.
details: Interviews zigzag toward saturation of categories.
concepts.recall_cue: What does each coding pass produce?

concepts.title: Action research
concepts.statement: Action research solves a real world issue while contributing to theory, with each cycle moving through plan, act, observe, and reflect.
details: Researchers design and measure change with the host organisation.
concepts.recall_cue: Why does this method carry two aims?

concepts.title: Ethnography
concepts.statement: Ethnography studies social interactions, behaviours, and perceptions within groups and communities by living among the people studied.
details: Interview and observation are triangulated because talk differs from action.

concepts.title: Case study
concepts.statement: A case study analyses a person, event, decision, project, or institution holistically as an instance of a class of phenomena.
details: Preferred for contemporary events when behaviour cannot be manipulated.
concepts.recall_cue: When does the case study win?

concepts.title: Four quality tests
concepts.statement: Guba and Lincoln's four tests of quality are credibility, dependability, transferability, and confirmability.
details: They replace statistical validity with assumptions of the qualitative paradigm.

relations.label: separates method from technique
relations.why: The distinction defines what a methodology does and does not cover.

relations.label: frames the qualitative stance
relations.why: A qualitative strategy of inquiry is what makes grounded theory available.

relations.label: needs coding to build theory
relations.why: Categories only become theory through the coding passes.

relations.label: theory-first versus problem-first
relations.why: Action research starts from a real world issue rather than from data alone.

relations.label: intervention versus observation
relations.why: Action research changes the setting while the case study studies it.

relations.label: culture versus bounded case
relations.why: Both observe in context but differ in the unit of analysis.

relations.label: interviews become case evidence
relations.why: Systematic interviewing feeds the case study evidence base.

relations.label: traceable categories aid credibility
relations.why: Credibility asks whether categories connect to the raw data.

relations.label: needs explicit quality tests
relations.why: Small samples make the four tests the argument for rigour.

logic_chain: Choose a strategy of inquiry for the research question.
Decide whether the question needs words, numbers, or both.
Select the method whose unit of analysis fits the question.
Collect data with interviews, focus groups, or observation.
Argue quality through the four alternative tests.

distinctions.rule: A method is an overall strategy; an interview or questionnaire only collects data inside it.
Ethnography follows a culture, while a case study bounds one instance of a phenomenon.

recall_prompts: Why is an interview not a method?
What do the three coding stages each produce?
Which four tests replace statistical validity in qualitative work?
